conceptual assets.concept: Sysinfo word 0 — reset-initialized CLOCK_FREQUENCY and bus-writable 32-bit word
conceptual assets.reasoning: The clocked process sysinfo_clk explicitly initializes and updates sysinfo(0): on reset `sysinfo(0) <= std_ulogic_vector(to_unsigned(CLOCK_FREQUENCY, 32))`; on rising_edge if `bus_req_i.stb = '1'` and `bus_req_i.rw = '1'` and `bus_req_i.addr(3 downto 2) = "00"` then `sysinfo(0) <= bus_req_i.data`. Readback uses the stored words: `bus_rsp_o.data <= sysinfo(to_integer(unsigned(buf_adr))) when (buf_ack = '1') else (others => '0')`. Therefore the correctness (integrity) of the 32-bit value held at sysinfo(0) is required for correct read responses. The declared internal signal sysinfo is the element that stores this word.

conceptual assets.concept: Sysinfo word 1 — reported memory/boot/hart configuration fields
conceptual assets.reasoning: Concurrent assignments build sysinfo(1) from declared generics/constants: `sysinfo(1)(7 downto 0) <= to_unsigned(log2_imem_size_c,8) when int_imem_en_c else ...`, `sysinfo(1)(15 downto 8) <= to_unsigned(log2_dmem_size_c,8) ...`, `sysinfo(1)(23 downto 16) <= std_ulogic_vector(to_unsigned(NUM_HARTS,8))`, `sysinfo(1)(31 downto 24) <= std_ulogic_vector(to_unsigned(BOOT_MODE_SELECT,8))`. Readback is via the same `bus_rsp_o.data <= sysinfo(to_integer(unsigned(buf_adr))) ...`. Thus integrity of the configuration fields reported in sysinfo(1) is established by the RTL. The declared internal signal sysinfo stores these fields.

conceptual assets.concept: Sysinfo word 2 — feature and I/O capability flags
conceptual assets.reasoning: Bits of sysinfo(2) are explicitly driven from feature-generics/constants (examples: `sysinfo(2)(0) <= '1' when INT_BOOTLOADER_EN else '0'`, `sysinfo(2)(11) <= '1' when OCD_AUTH else '0'`, `sysinfo(2)(15) <= '1' when IO_GPIO_EN else '0'`, etc.). These bits are returned to the bus via `bus_rsp_o.data <= sysinfo(to_integer(unsigned(buf_adr))) when (buf_ack='1') ...`. The RTL therefore establishes that the integrity of the capability/flag word sysinfo(2) matters for correct reporting. The declared internal signal sysinfo stores this word.

conceptual assets.concept: Sysinfo word 3 — cache geometry fields (block size and block counts)
conceptual assets.reasoning: Concurrent assignments drive sysinfo(3) from cache-related constants and enables (examples: `sysinfo(3)(3 downto 0) <= to_unsigned(log2_c_bsize_c,4) when ICACHE_EN else (others => '0')`, `sysinfo(3)(7 downto 4) <= to_unsigned(log2_ic_bnum_c,4) when ICACHE_EN else (others => '0')`, etc.). These fields are returned by the read path `bus_rsp_o.data <= sysinfo(to_integer(unsigned(buf_adr))) ...`, so the RTL establishes integrity of the cache-geometry word. The declared internal signal sysinfo stores this word.

conceptual assets.concept: Buffered bus request capture — the stored address and ack that select and enable sysinfo read responses
conceptual assets.reasoning: The access_buffer process captures and retains request state: on reset `buf_ack <= '0'` and `buf_adr <= (others => '0')`; on rising_edge `buf_ack <= bus_req_i.stb; if (bus_req_i.stb = '1') then buf_adr <= bus_req_i.addr(3 downto 2); end if;`. The read-response logic uses those buffers: `bus_rsp_o.data <= sysinfo(to_integer(unsigned(buf_adr))) when (buf_ack = '1') else (others => '0')` and `bus_rsp_o.ack <= buf_ack`. Hence buf_adr and buf_ack decide which sysinfo word is returned and whether an ack/data are presented; corruption or suppression of these stored values would violate correct selection/delivery (integrity and availability of responses). These buffers are stored in the declared internal signals buf_adr and buf_ack.
